task_id: R-01 / conditional unused-chip CS pull-up feasibility
status: Engineering proposal only; no resistor installed, no chip/host interaction in this step
owner_inventory: Owner confirms no resistors; asks whether Pi can supply variable resistance. Existing Dupont leads and spare full-size clips; breadboard/secure connection not confirmed.

Pi_substitute.decision: No suitable GPIO/software-only substitute for a passive pull-up to the flash rail.
Pi_substitute.reason: RP1 pad settings enable pull-up/down and drive strength; they do not supply a configurable two-terminal resistor to an external 1.8 V rail. Pi 5 GPIO runs at 3.3 V; direct weak pull-up may overvoltage the flash if loading changes. Changing RP1 threshold registers does not change its physical supply.

conditional_topology.active_programmer_clip: Existing short clip on U2 through checked 1.8 V adapter; unchanged.
conditional_topology.auxiliary_access: If both clips fit without stress, use spare full SOIC-16 clip on U1 with independently checked physical pin-to-terminal mapping. Only two leads used; other contacts externally disconnected/insulated.
conditional_topology.connection: U1 physical pin 2/VCC -> resistor -> U1 physical pin 7/CS. This uses the existing target 1.8 V rail, not Pi 3.3 V/5 V.
conditional_topology.pin_number_warning: Physical 16-pin Micron package numbers, not adapter OUTPUT numbers or assumed ribbon order.
conditional_topology.purpose: Bias unused U1 CS high while U2 is selected; this is not physical isolation and may fail against board loading.

candidate_first_diagnostic.component: Through-hole fixed 10 kOhm resistor, 1/4 W, preferably 1% (5% also suitable after measurement). Small solderless breadboard provides secure Dupont/resistor connection.
candidate_first_diagnostic.basis: Conservative bounded added-current starting experiment, not inferred from unpowered 4.35/4.8 kOhm equivalents or claimed vendor-approved Cisco repair. Unknown board paths mean efficacy/safety cannot be guaranteed solely from resistor current.
candidate_first_diagnostic.not_selected: No lower-resistance escalation, variable-potentiometer wiper, direct CS-to-VCC jumper, Pi pull-up or added power source.

staged_checks: Obtain actual resistor and secure connection. Confirm spare clip and two clips physically fit before attachment.

Before wiring, reconfirm chassis/U2 and isolation/ownership; shut down/unplug Pi, verify zero residual voltage; verify resistor value, clip mapping and absence of unintended shorts. No under-clip or fine-mux probing.
Power only the checked Pi/adapter setup; check P1 supply and unused U1 CS with no clock/bytes. Verify resistor is connected to the flash rail.

Only if idle readings acceptable, use bounded no-clock U2 select-only control and meter unused U1 CS plus supply. Observe selected U2 CS low at an accessible checked endpoint if available. Stop if unused CS does not remain convincingly high; do not just decrease resistor value.
Passing DC control would justify only conditional bounded multi-address/transfer-shape reads with comparison against preserved references, not a firmware write or whole-array accuracy claim.
limits: No resistor exists in current inventory, so no wiring/test can proceed yet.
A pull-up test measures response to a known limited load; it cannot identify a specific active driver or prove complete electrical isolation.
DMM spot measurements do not certify fast transitions/clocked signal margins.
If secure bias/control cannot be established, separately read chips off-board using suitable rework assistance; do not recommend inexperienced leg lifting/trace cutting.

sources.support: RP1 GPIO supply bank, pad PUE/PDE and DRIVE controls; input threshold warning.
Micron Figure 6 physical pinout, Table 1 CS high tri-states output, Table 47 thresholds, 1.7–2.0 V operating rail.

next_step: Current photos show both flash packages bare. First establish present power/clip/ownership and confirm U1pin7 physical endpoint against IMG_1289; no substitute pickup or grabber fit verified. Resistor experiment remains conditional.

access_revision.owner_concern: Two full clips may not fit on U1 and U2 simultaneously; asks whether parts should still be ordered.
access_revision.finding: Two full clips are optional. Only one secure connection to unused U1 pin7/CS is essential; source rail can be obtained from already mapped P1 pin1/VCC. No direct header CS contact has been established: historical P1pin8 paths are kilohm references, not CS continuity.
access_revision.alternative_topology: P1 physical pin1/VCC (existing target ~1.8 V rail) -> fixed 10 kOhm resistor/breadboard -> suitable insulated single-leg IC micrograbber -> unused U1 physical pin7/CS; programming clip remains on U2.
access_revision.limits: Meter access to bare U1pin7 exists, but secure grabber contact/clearance has not been validated. Historical IMG_1277 was inspected as geometry reference only; it shows an earlier clip arrangement and cannot certify current fit. No new photo or physical check performed.
access_revision.procurement: Resistor/breadboard remain useful for either topology. Hold final order until a suitable single-leg grabber/lead and current clearance are checked, so buying the passive parts alone does not imply readiness. No additional full SOIC clip needed for this alternative.

candidate_connector_reference.facts: XKM has narrow double-hook nose and 0.025 inch square connection pins. This is a candidate style/connector reference, not verified physical fit on this chassis.

access_revision.next_information: Current close-up showing U1, U2 and the programming clip in place, plus chosen grabber dimensions/product link, can support a fit decision without moving wiring or trying two clips powered.

owner_parts_update: Intends to order breadboard and 1% 1/2W resistor assortment including ten10kOhm parts; not received. Secure access remains unresolved.
